newsitem.title: MALAYSIA: Malaysia's Mahathir returns to simmering scandals.
newsitem.headline: Malaysia's Mahathir returns to simmering scandals.

text.p: Malaysian Prime Minister Mahathir Mohamad returns home on Wednesday to a cauldron of simmering scandals in his government after a two-week trip abroad promoting "Malaysia, Inc".
Analysts said half a dozen brewing scandals would test Mahathir's credibility after he last year made a big issue of "money politics", which covers a host of corruption sins.

Last week, Deputy Prime Minister Anwar Ibrahim stunned the business community by announcing an investigation into a tender awarded by the state-run telephone firm Telekom Malaysia to Sweden's LM Ericcson more than four years ago.

Then on a visit to the north Borneo state of Sabah on Monday, Anwar vowed to get to the bottom of a suspected log smuggling operation after a Japan-bound ship was intercepted with a cargo of logs worth six million ringgit ($2.40 million).
Anwar said six other ships carrying illegal logs escaped.
Disappearing forests are worrying Sanusi Junid, the new Chief Minister of Mahathir's home state of Kedah.
The Star newspaper reported on Tuesday Sanusi has ordered a probe into why some 17,000 hectares (42,000 acres) of gazetted forest land was either sold or given away to certain parties.
On Friday, Primary Industries Minister Lim Keng Yaik denied that he had received special stock shares reserved for ethnic Malays.

Lim threatened to sue his accuser, a former senior official in the Ministry of International Trade and Industry, which runs the programme. The official, Rejab Lebai Man, is himself on trial charged with illegally receiving special shares.
Trade and Industry Minister Rafidah Aziz was investigated by the Anti-Corruption Agency last year in a similar case but was cleared by Mahathir.

In the most publicised case recently, Muhammad Muhammad Taib, a vice president of Mahathir's United Malays National Organisation (UMNO) and chief minister of central Selangor state, was detained at Australia's Brisbane airport for bringing in some $900,000 in undeclared currency in a suitcase.
He said the cash was to buy property on behalf of his brothers. He was freed on bail.
The rash of incidents followed a tearful speech by Mahathir to delegates at UMNO's election convention last October to reject candidates who practised "money politics".

"People will be watching this latest group of scandals to see how the Prime Minister reacts after his emotional speech to the party last October," said Bruce Gale, regional director of the Hong Kong-based Political & Economic Risk Consultancy.
Mahathir is returning from a two-week trip to the United States and Japan promoting his latest brainchild, an investment zone for global multimedia companies.
Mahathir has defended the government's close links with business as part of his "Malaysia Inc" programme.
One key question is to what extent Mahathir backs Anwar's efforts to root out scandal and corruption in the business-government nexus, analysts said.
It was Anwar who last year first spilled the beans in parliament about the biggest scandal of them all -- seven billion ringgit in accumulated liabilities at state-owned Perwaja Steel.
An audit firm said some of the losses at Perwaja, a pet project of Mahathir's, were due to financial mismanagement and irregularities.
No one from Perwaja has been charged with a crime and the government has assumed its debts and accumulated losses.
"These other scandals are small brush fires compared with Perwaja," Gale said. "If Mahathir is not seen as coming down hard on Perwaja, why should people take him seriously in other areas?"
